I worry about everything: the schedule at the site, whether the guys are safe, money, my wife’s health, even little stuff like paying bills on time. It’s not just stress in the moment—it’s there when I wake up, during work, even when I’m trying to watch TV at night. I’ve tried relaxing, walking away, even my wife tells me to “just chill,” but I can’t seem to control it.  

The past six months especially, I’ve been jumping at sounds—like a tool dropping or a truck backfiring—and my body’s always tense. My back aches constantly, and my shoulders and legs feel worn out like I’ve been lifting all day, even when I haven’t.  

Yeah, things have been rough—my dad passed last year, and work’s been busy—but honestly, the worrying started before any of that and never really let up. It’s like it’s just part of me now, no matter what’s going on around me.
D011-D020_h001.question_b:

My mind races about things I never used to stress over—money, my kids’ future, even whether I locked the truck at work. I try to shut it off, but the thoughts just won’t stop. Little sounds—a hammer dropping, a radio blasting—make me jump like I’ve been shocked. My back and shoulders are always tight, and my arms and legs ache even after light days. It’s not like an injury—more like my whole body is wound up.

It all started within weeks of my dad’s funeral. Before that, yeah, life was busy, but I handled it fine. Now, I can trace every bit of this back to that loss. My wife says I’ve changed—shorter fuse, can’t relax. I know it’s connected to what happened. I don’t feel anxious all the time about everything—I feel it because of this.
